speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you tell me how long you have had this and if it is itchy, painful, or oozing?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pityriasis Capitis (Seborrheic Dermatitis).

The family history of psoriasis and the "red, scaly" nature of the rash in an infant are classic presentations for infantile seborrheic dermatitis, often called "cradle cap" when on the scalp. Since the baby was born prematurely and has been generally healthy, this is likely a common, benign condition. Do you see any signs of crusting or hair loss at the site?
